title: Three outages, three failure modes, three recovery curves
description: The point of this scenario is that 'an acquirer went down' is at least three different events and a benchmark that ran only one of them has tested one third of the logic. timeout leaves the result UNKNOWN (#10's double-charge case); connection_refused is a fast, certain error with the same routing consequence and none of the ambiguity; decline_storm is not an outage at all from the engine's side -- the acquirer is up, answering, and every answer is a soft decline, which is exactly the case a health model that only counts timeouts gets wrong. The recoveries differ the same way: step, exponential (tau 900s), linear.
